name: Customer Churn and Exit Interview Mining
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that customers abandon [incumbent solution category] because of [deficiency X]. We will verify this by auditing 20 canceled customer accounts or exit interviews, and consider it validated if ≥ 50% identify [deficiency X] as their primary non-negotiable exit driver rather than pricing or budget constraints.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Pull accounts cancelled in the last 30 to 60 days; frame the call as a process post-mortem, not a win-back.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Ask when value stopped, what workaround they built before leaving, and what replaced the product.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Code each exit into price, product defect, reorganisation or loss of internal champion.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Extract lists of accounts canceled within the prior 30–60 days. Frame interview outreach as an operational post-mortem aimed at process improvement rather than customer win-back.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Conduct 20-minute structured exit interviews inquiring: "At what specific moment did the product cease delivering anticipated value?" "What workaround did you build prior to cancellation?" "What replacement system was deployed?"

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Code exit rationales into root categories: price sensitivity, core product defect, organizational reorganization, or loss of internal champion.

warning.label: Scapegoat Rationalization
warning.text: Churned clients blame price or a peripheral bug rather than admit the organisation could not adopt it.

warningFull: Churned clients routinely point to price or peripheral software bugs as polite covers rather than acknowledging their organization lacked the operational competence to adopt the platform.
